newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end in retreat but off lows.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end in retreat but off lows.

text.p: French shares finished a nervous session in loss on Wednesday but off the lows as a rising Dow rode to the rescue in the afternoon.
Traders said Paris dipped to a loss of 1.5 percent as the markets whipsawed after a U.S. durable goods report showed a 1.7 percent fall instead of an expected increase.
Profit-taking and a softer dollar also added pressure on the CAC 40 index, which was consolidating recent big gains.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 17.75 points or 0.71 percent at 2,465.01. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 19.5 at 2,465 from Tuesday's close.
Volume was a hefty 7.79 billion francs.

The rally in Paris seen since the start of the year has taken the market to historic highs but risks running out of steam as profit-taking kicks in, making it likely to stay flat until the second half, analysts said.
Bryan Allworth at Merrill Lynch expects the CAC-40 to be at 2,400 in three months' time, rising to 2,700 at the end of the year, implying a correction in the coming weeks.
"I don't see a real improvement until the end of the second quarter or in the second half. There have to be some really good corporate earnings to justify the current levels," he said.

Bouygues jumped 3.79 percent to 548 francs as some brokers welcomed 1996 results which came in better than expected. But others said it was hard to see what exactly was treated as exceptional and recurring gains.
Paris Capital Markets confirmed it went to buy from neutral.
Danone denied market talk it was poised to sell its bottling or beer activities, rumours which some brokers said may have been behind a 1.36 percent rise to 822.
After the close the food and drinks company posted an eight percent rise in 1996 net income to 3.38 billion francs after restating its 1995 results to take a restructuring charge.
TV station TF1 fell four percent to 486.3, as brokers pointed to declines in profit, market share and advertising.
